active_family: 51-channel joint IV+factor panel transition feasibility probe
current_bottleneck: Joint IV+factor panel training now works mechanically at 30-day and 90-day horizons, but it is not yet a validated risk-deck replacement. The remaining bottlenecks are a first-class missing-data/transform manifest for heterogeneous factors, an official IV-subpanel evaluation for the 30-day checkpoint, and horizon-specific metrics for 60/90/152/252-day use.
last_result_summary: 571 trained the existing 537a 51-channel daily panel transition law on recent windows for both h30 and h90. The h30 run used 512 train windows and 441 validation windows with best_val_nll 1.1407808321; the h90 run used the same panel with best_val_nll 1.0971591096. Both checkpoints sampled finite 51-channel paths with finite_rate 1.0. This proves joint/horizon mechanical feasibility, not risk-manager quality.
next_step_recommendation: Before full-scale joint deployment, formalize factor preprocessing: no silent structural zero fills for missing factor levels, record per-factor source/transform/unit, and decide between start-date truncation versus documented bfill/ffill. Then run an official 30-day IV-subpanel suite on the 571a checkpoint and define separate long-horizon factor/IV realism metrics.
current_best_note: 510a remains the best base learned law at 8/11. 564a/568a/570a is still the constrained risk-manager deployable IV prototype. 571 proves joint IV+factor h30/h90 training feasibility but has not yet beaten or replaced the validated IV frontier.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
